title: Inverted Pendulum in the Sky: Floquet Stabilization of Cosmological Axions
comment: 16 pages, 8 figures, 1 table
summary: Many cosmological scenarios require a scalar field to sit near the top of its potential, which usually requires a fine-tuned initial condition. We ask whether the hilltop of an axion potential can be dynamically stabilized by a rapidly oscillating coupling, as for the inverted pendulum of Kapitza, and to what extent this can reduce the fine-tuning. Using Floquet theory, we determine the stability window of the hilltop and analyze several realizations: an oscillating coupling, a spinning or oscillating second field, and a gyroscopic analogue, an inverted spinning top realized by a sigma model on a squashed three-sphere. In an expanding Universe the stabilized phase lasts for a number of $e$-folds logarithmic in the hierarchy of scales, independently of the cosmological background. Classifying the stabilizers by how their effective frequency redshifts, we show that in these realizations the hilltop cannot both attract the field and leave it frozen by the Hubble friction during radiation or matter domination, and that during inflation the attraction is limited by the Hubble friction and the energy budget. Thus the simple realizations studied here do not generically remove the hilltop fine-tuning. They can instead delay the onset of the oscillation and enhance the relic abundance as $n_φ/n_{φ,{\rm std}}\propto(\tilde m/H_c)^{3/2}$ in radiation domination. We discuss the implications for axion dark matter, inflation, quintessence and curvatons.

title: Binary mass transfer fossil in the ancient GD-1 stellar stream
comment: 15 pages, 7 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for publication in ApJL
summary: We report the discovery of J0930+2902, the first carbon-enhanced metal-poor star with s-process enrichment (CEMP-s) identified in the GD-1 stellar stream, which is widely believed to originate from the tidal disruption of an old, metal-poor globular cluster. Using high-resolution Subaru/HDS spectroscopy, we present a comprehensive chemical abundance analysis of this star. Stellar atmospheric parameters were re-derived using Gaia photometry and parallaxes, combined with an iterative non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) analysis of Fe lines. We determine abundances for 22 elements, including NLTE analyses of C, Na, Mg, Ca, Ti, Cr, Mn, Co, Sr, Y, Zr, Ba, and Eu. J0930+2902 exhibits pronounced enhancements of C, N, Na, and s-process elements, together with a low $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratio of 7.4, consistent with enrichment through binary mass transfer from a former asymptotic giant branch (AGB) companion. Large radial-velocity variations and a significant near-ultraviolet excess independently indicate the presence of a white dwarf companion, providing strong support for this scenario. Comparisons with FRUITY AGB nucleosynthesis models show that the residual neutron-capture abundance pattern is best reproduced by a low-mass AGB companion with an initial mass of approximately 3.0 $M_{\odot}$. Its enhancements of C, N, Na, and s-process elements make it chemically distinct from the other confirmed GD-1 members. These results identify J0930+2902 as a fossil record of binary mass transfer preserved in the ancient GD-1 stellar stream, demonstrating that binary interaction can leave long-lived chemical signatures in accreted stellar populations.

title: Multiwavelength Analysis of the Merging Cluster RM J121917.6+505432.8: A Three-way Merger in Disguise?
comment: 26 pages, 13 figures
summary: We identify the galaxy cluster RM J121917.6+505432.8 as a candidate bimodal merging cluster due to its optical properties listed in the redMaPPer cluster catalog. To confirm the cluster's merging state and reveal its dark matter halo and intracluster medium (ICM) morphologies, we conducted a multiwavelength follow-up campaign encompassing HST/ACS optical observations, XMM-Newton X-ray imaging, and Keck/Deimos multislit spectroscopy. The weak lensing mass reconstruction performed with the HST images shows two resolved peaks whose positions coincide with the two brightest cluster galaxies. The ICM morphology is consistent with a post-pericenter merger, with significant asymmetry in X-ray flux between subclusters. Our Keck/Deimos redshift measurements reveal a relative velocity $Δv_{\mathrm{LOS}} = 480$ km s$^{-1}$ between eastern and western subclusters. The eastern, more massive subcluster, however, exhibits a highly elongated shape, suggesting either a dark matter halo of considerable eccentricity or the presence of a third, unresolved halo, eliciting the question of whether RMJ1219 is truly binary or a three-way merger. To investigate these hypotheses, we fit the weak lensing shear data using four different combinations of spherical and elliptical NFW halo models and provide an estimate of the mass and concentration of each subhalo. Although the best fit is achieved with a three-halo model, the data are insufficient to determine whether the introduction of extra parameters is statistically justified.

title: UNIONS and Euclid: Calibrating point source-galaxy separation for ground-based surveys
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A. Some material is available online on https://github.com/GFThomas/StarGal_ground_Euclid
summary: Efficient separation of unresolved point sources from extended objects (star-galaxy separation) is essential for deep wide-field imaging surveys, particularly at faint magnitudes where morphological differences become subtle. We assess two morphology-based classification methods applied to single-band, ground-based imaging from the Ultraviolet Near-Infrared Optical Northern Survey (UNIONS), using Euclid observations as a high-fidelity reference to evaluate their performance and to train one of the methods. We analysed 8 deg$^2$ of overlapping UNIONS $r$-band and Euclid $I_E$ data, comprising more than $7\times10^{5}$ sources. The Euclid data enable robust morphological labelling down to $I_E\simeq 26$, which we used to train and validate two classification approaches applied to UNIONS alone: a curve-of-growth method and a supervised neural-network classifier, both based on aperture photometry and image-quality information. The curve-of-growth method yields an almost perfectly complete point-source sample ($>95\%$), but its purity decreases rapidly at $r \simeq 22.5$. The neural-network approach significantly improves the purity at the faint end, maintaining $\geq 80\%$ purity down to $r \simeq 24$, while the completeness decreases to almost $50\%$ at similar depths. In both cases, performance strongly depends on the image quality of the ground-based data. This work shows how Euclid data can be used to develop, calibrate, and validate star-galaxy separation methods for ground-based surveys, useful in regions not covered by Euclid. Both methods have already been applied to UNIONS data and are readily applicable to future surveys such as LSST, offering flexible solutions depending on whether completeness or purity is prioritised.

title: Halo spin-axis correlations in IllustrisTNG: Lagrangian-to-Eulerian separation mapping, baryonic effects, and redshift-space distortions
comment: 33 pages, 15 figures, 4 tables
summary: We investigate correlations of halo and stellar spin axes in the TNG300 volume of the IllustrisTNG simulations and compare them with a model based on linear tidal torque theory (LTTT). Dark matter (DM) halo spin axes at $z = 0$ exhibit positive correlations as a function of Lagrangian pair separation. The LTTT-based model describes their separation dependence well, with weak variation in the fitted amplitude across mass thresholds. A Lagrangian-to-Eulerian separation mapping based on the conditional distributions of initial separations at fixed present-day separation, measured directly from the simulations, allows the model to reproduce the overall trends in both real and redshift space without additional fitting. The hydrodynamic and DM-only runs generally show similar DM halo spin-axis correlations, although the DM-only run exhibits a steeper rise at small real-space separations. In the hydrodynamic run, stellar spin-axis correlations are consistent with the same Lagrangian form as their DM halo counterparts, but with approximately 60% of the DM correlation amplitudes. Positive stellar correlations persist in both real and redshift space, and the mapped model captures their separation dependence. Initial spin-axis correlations of protohalos are substantially stronger than their present-day counterparts at the same Lagrangian separations, consistent with subsequent nonlinear spin evolution weakening these correlations. These results suggest that present-day halo and stellar spin-axis correlations retain signatures of the initial tidal field and that their general behavior can be understood through LTTT-based modeling combined with pair-separation mapping.

title: Characterization and empirical correction of a spatially coherent spectral artifact in Gemini/GMOS-N IFU observations
summary: We report a recurring spectral artifact identified in observations obtained with the integral field unit (IFU) of the Gemini Multi-Object Spectrograph on the Gemini North telescope (GMOS-N). The artifact appears as a vertically aligned structure in reconstructed images of the IFU field of view, associated with a specific group of fibers and exhibiting a broad spectral feature around 8000~\AAng. Similar features were repeatedly identified in observations of different astronomical targets obtained between 2020 and 2022 using the R150 grating in the two-slit IFU mode. Taking advantage of the reproducibility of the artifact in the fiber and wavelength domains, we develop an empirical correction method in which the artifact is modeled as the product of a common spectral profile and a fiber-dependent amplitude distribution, with an overall normalization determined independently for each exposure. The artifact template is constructed from observations in which the affected fibers are largely separated from the astronomical source and subsequently applied to independent observations in which the artifact overlaps the source. The correction substantially suppresses the artificial spatial structure in the reconstructed images. Although the physical origin of the artifact remains unidentified, we present its observational characteristics and correction procedure to facilitate the identification and treatment of similar features by other GMOS-IFU users.

title: An oxygen-rich supernova remnant in NGC 253 with narrow [N II] emission lines
comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, accepted for publication in A&A
summary:
Context. Supernova remnants (SNRs) are the final evolutionary stage of supernovae. In rare cases, the remnant persists as an optically luminous remnant decades after the explosion. We report the discovery of an unusual oxygen-rich (O-rich) SNR that was serendipitously discovered in the MUSE mosaic of the nearby (D $\sim$ 3.5 Mpc) galaxy NGC 253 released by arXiv:2506.14921.
  Aims. We search for SNRs in MUSE integral field spectroscopy data of NGC 253.
  Methods. We search for unresolved point sources with broad and strong [O III]$λ$$λ$4959,5007, [O I]$λ$$λ$6300,6364 or [O II]$λ$$λ$7320,7331 emission lines. We also search for possible counterparts at other wavelengths in archival data.
  Results. We find a single O-rich SNR in NGC 253 with [O III]$λ$$λ$4959,5007. For this object, we report a coincident X-ray source detected by Chandra and a non-detection at mid-infrared wavelengths by JWST. Additionally, we identify [N II]$λ$$λ$6548,6583 emission lines and no detectable hydrogen or [SII]$λ$$λ$6716,6731 emission. The [N II] emission lines are broader (230 km/s) than the surrounding interstellar medium lines but still narrow in comparison to the [O III] emission (>1500 km/s) from the SNR. No detections of [O I]$λ$$λ$6300,6364 and [O II]$λ$$λ$7320,7331 were made.
  Conclusions. The discovery of a single O-rich SNR after a systematic search of NGC 253 highlights their scarcity in nearby galaxies. The structure of [O III] emission indicates complex structure in the O-rich ejecta. The relative narrowness of [N II] emission lines compared to the [O III] lines and the non-detection of hydrogen show that the remnant is surrounded by an N-rich circumstellar medium. The ejecta is currently interacting with this material of the preceding supernova explosion.

title: Optical Light-Curve Broadening in the Redback Binary PSR J2215+5135
summary: Spider millisecond pulsars offer a direct route to constrain neutron-star masses, including candidates above two solar masses, via optical light-curve modeling of the irradiated companion. This assumes stable irradiation. We report new $g'r'i'$ photometry of the redback PSR~J2215+5135 from the Iranian National Observatory in 2024 and compare it with the 2014 data of \citet{linares2018peering}. Peak brightness and orbital period are unchanged within uncertainties, but the light-curve wings are significantly broader in 2024, as the local deviations exceed $3σ$ on the rising branch in all filters, with an additional $i'$-band excess on the falling branch, giving a global permutation-test significance of $4.26σ$. A single-hot-spot model fits the 2024 data better than a spot-free one, but systematic residuals remain. The broader wings are reproduced only through correlated shifts in the spot, inclination, filling factor and companion temperature, which we regard as model compensation, not physics. An extended, variable heating component may also fit. The best-fit spot temperature differs between epochs by about $1060$\,K, comparable to its model dependence (about $900$\,K between two codes for 2014), so we do not interpret this as physical. Two epochs cannot show whether the change is gradual, sudden or short-lived. The inferred neutron-star mass depends on the spot treatment: $2.13^{+0.16}_{-0.13}\,M_\odot$ for 2014 with a hot spot, and $M_\mathrm{NS}=1.95^{+0.11}_{-0.07}\,M_\odot$ for 2024. These agree within about $1σ$, but come from differently shaped light curves, and the statistical uncertainties exclude heating-prescription systematics.

title: A Chandra X-Ray Survey of the Middle-aged Supernova Remnant G22.7-0.2 Interacting with Molecular Clouds
comment: 17 pages, 8 figures, 3 tables; submitted to AAS Journals
summary: G22.7$-$0.2 is a middle-aged supernova remnant (SNR; $τ\sim 3\times10^4$ yr) interacting with the nearby giant molecular cloud GMC 23.3$-$0.4. A handful of X-ray sources have been identified within the SNR radio shell by previous XMM-Newton and NuSTAR observations. In particular, three of those X-ray sources (N1, N2, and N3) have been detected above 10 keV, indicating that they are either X-ray point sources, or molecular cloud clumps heated by SNR blast waves. In the latter case, non-thermal bremsstrahlung or synchrotron radiation from shock-heated molecular clouds may appear as extended X-ray sources. We conducted an X-ray survey of the SNR-cloud interaction region with Chandra and detected 23 X-ray sources with $> 5σ$ significance using wavdetect, 20 of which were previously uncataloged. The sub-arcsecond angular resolution of Chandra allowed us to spatially resolve these X-ray sources. After accounting for point spread function (PSF) smearing and dust scattering effects, we determine that two NuSTAR hard X-ray sources (N1 and N2) are extended, whereas the other Chandra sources are point sources. While N1 may be a compact filament or a synchrotron-emitting clump with $r\sim0.018$ pc, our analysis suggests that N2 is likely a compact cloud clump shock-heated by the SNR and emitting non-thermal bremsstrahlung or synchrotron X-rays, with $r\sim0.052$ pc and $M\approx0.6$ $M_\odot$ under the non-thermal bremsstrahlung model.

title: A search and multi-frequency study of curved parsec-scale jets in active galaxies
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A. 15 pages, 14 figures, 4 tables
summary: Very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) observations show that a fraction of active galactic nucleus (AGN) jets exhibit pronounced apparent bending on parsec scales, potentially strongly enhanced by projection effects. While individual sources have been studied in detail, the statistical properties of curved jets and the physical mechanisms responsible for their morphology remain poorly constrained. We aim to select a statistically robust sample of AGNs with significantly curved parsec-scale jets and to constrain the physical mechanisms responsible for jet bending. We analyse 123 456 VLBI images of 17 478 AGNs collected by the public Astrogeo database. After filtering for extended structure, we extract and stack multi-epoch, multi-frequency (1.2--86 GHz) ridge lines. We fit linear and logarithmic helices representing jet precession and resonant Kelvin--Helmholtz instability mode. We combine model-fits and Monte Carlo simulations to further constrain these physical models. We robustly identify 586 AGNs (7.4% of sources with resolved jets) with curved parsec-scale jets. Compared to straight jets, curved ones are less common at low redshifts, possibly due to the sample-related selection effects. In the precession scenario, the inferred periods span $P \sim$10--10 000 yr, with a logarithmic mean of $\sim 220$ yr. Solid-body disc precession in supermassive black hole binaries is broadly consistent with these periods, whereas geodetic precession requires extremely tight, near-equal-mass systems. Lense--Thirring precession remains viable for both thin and thick discs. Kelvin--Helmholtz instability also provides a potential explanation. However, identifying the preferred model for each individual source requires further investigation, including temporal analysis and jet kinematics.

title: Comprehensive In Situ Characterization of Amorphous Solid Water Films with COSPINU2 set-up: Optical Properties, Density, Morphology, and Restructuring Dynamics
comment: The following article has been accepted by Review of Scientific Instruments. After it is published, it will be found at aip.org
summary: Amorphous solid water (ASW) dominates interstellar ice mantles, but its porosity, density, optical response, and mechanical stability depend sensitively on how the ice is grown. Here, we present the characterization capabilities of COSPINU2, a cryogenic ultra-high-vacuum set-up designed to prepare and diagnose water ice films under controlled background and doser-assisted deposition conditions. The instrument combines a calibrated gas-handling line, near- and mid-infrared Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, HeNe interferometry, broad-beam optical imaging, and quadrupole mass spectrometry. We demonstrate how these complementary diagnostics provide a coherent description of ASW films grown between 10K and 150K. For background-grown ices, a dual-angle interferometric method is used to retrieve refractive indices near 632 nm, while near-infrared interference fringes provide thickness calibration. The results show that lower deposition temperatures and higher growth rates produce films with lower refractive indices and stronger dangling-OH infrared signatures, consistent with the formation of more porous ASW. We also show that pressure-based density estimates are unreliable in the background geometry because cryopumping decouple chamber pressure from the local substrate flux. For doser-grown films, optical interference imaging allows reconstruction of dome-shaped thickness profiles and estimation of effective densities. Finally, sudden restructuring events are observed in thick (above 2 micrometers), low-temperature porous ASW films, evidenced by abrupt changes in interferometric contrast, optical scattering, and dangling-OH features. These results establish COSPINU2 as a versatile platform for quantitative water-ice characterization and provide the physical baseline required for future studies of infrared irradiation and optical constants of interstellar ice analogues.
